title: Clojure
subtitle: A modern Lisp on the Java platform built around immutable data, plain maps and a live REPL, from a first program to professional practice.
description: Clojure is a dynamic, functional dialect of Lisp that Rich Hickey released in 2007. It runs on the Java Virtual Machine and can call any Java library, and its sister language ClojureScript compiles to JavaScript. Its defining ideas are immutable, persistent data structures; programs built from small functions over plain maps and vectors; a small set of carefully designed tools for managing state that changes over time; and a workflow in which you grow a program inside a running REPL instead of restarting it after every edit. It is used for web services and back-end systems, data processing, financial software (a large Brazilian bank, Nubank, runs much of its business on it) and anywhere a team values simple, data-oriented code.

This course is for anyone who already knows what a variable, a loop and a function are: the Start level of [Lumenary CS](/en/cs/) or equivalent experience in any language. No Lisp or Java experience is assumed. It starts with the parentheses and the REPL, works through immutable data, functions, sequences and data-oriented design, and ends with state and concurrency, Java interop, macros, testing, the tools professionals use every day and a complete small project.

To run the code, install a Java runtime and the Clojure CLI by following the official guide at [clojure.org/guides/install_clojure](https://clojure.org/guides/install_clojure); save a program as `main.clj` and run it with `clojure -M main.clj`, or start a REPL with `clj`. Clojure has no official online playground. Every complete program in these lessons was run with Clojure 1.12 on Java 21 by Lumenary's test suite, using only the core library, and the output shown is the output it printed. The lessons were drafted with AI assistance and are awaiting review by a human computer scientist.

levels.title: Foundations
levels.summary: Install the Clojure CLI, read and write Lisp syntax at the REPL, and learn the core of the language: immutable collections, functions, control flow and destructuring.

levels.title: Practice
levels.summary: Transform data with lazy sequences and transducers, model a domain with plain maps, namespaces, protocols and spec, and manage changing state with atoms, refs and agents.

levels.title: Professional
levels.summary: Use the Java platform from Clojure, handle errors and write macros with care, test with clojure.test, know the tools and the ClojureScript side of the ecosystem, and build a complete project.
